If you have standing water, soggy lawn areas, or water pooling near your foundation, a French drain is often the right solution — we assess this during your free consultation.

items.q: How much does countertop installation cost in Denver?
items.a: Cost depends on the material you choose, the size of your countertop area, the edge profile, and the number of cutouts needed. Quartz and solid surface options are generally more consistent in pricing, while granite varies by slab. We provide a free, detailed estimate after measuring your space.

items.q: How long does countertop installation take?
items.a: Most countertop installations are completed in a single day once fabrication is finished. The fabrication process typically takes [X] business days after your measurements and material selection are confirmed — we’ll give you an exact timeline during your consultation.

items.q: What is the difference between quartz and granite countertops?
items.a: Granite is a 100% natural stone quarried from the earth — every slab is one-of-a-kind with unique veining and patterns. Quartz is an engineered stone made from natural quartz crystals and resin — it’s non-porous, highly stain-resistant, and consistent in color and pattern. Both are durable, beautiful, and long-lasting; the right choice depends on your lifestyle, aesthetic preference, and how much maintenance you want to do.

items.q: Do quartz countertops stain?
items.a: Quartz is non-porous and highly resistant to staining, making it an excellent choice for kitchens. It does not require sealing and is easier to maintain than natural stone. Granite and marble are more porous and should be sealed periodically to maintain stain resistance.

items.q: Do you remove and dispose of old countertops?
items.a: Yes. We handle complete removal of your existing countertops, prep the space, and dispose of the old material as part of our full-service installation — no separate contractor needed.

items.q: Can you install an undermount sink as part of the project?
items.a: Yes. We handle all sink cutouts — undermount, drop-in, and farmhouse styles — as part of the fabrication and installation process.

items.q: Are your countertop installers licensed and insured?
items.a: Yes. JRC Countertops operates under JRC Home Remodeling’s full licensing and insurance, protecting your home and our team throughout every installation.
